title: The Adventures of Mercury Ali of Cairo

keywords: the adventures of mercury ali of cairo
full_text:
Ali Zaybaq—known across the East as 'Mercury Ali' because of his lightning agility and slippery cunning—was a noble-hearted rogue of Cairo who used his wits exclusively to protect poor artisans and defend the helpless against tyrannical officials.

Hearing of Dalilah’s fame in Baghdad, Ali traveled to the Abbasid capital to test his skills against the masters of Iraq.

Ali entered the fortified palace of the corrupt Chief of the Watch, who had extorted gold from the market weavers. Scaling the eighty-foot stone tower with silk ropes and suction cups, Ali entered the treasury, gathered the extorted gold, lowered it to the street, and distributed every single coin back to the poor weavers before dawn, leaving his silver signature mark—a running quail—carved upon the chief’s desk!

The Caliph Harun al-Rashid, amused and impressed by Ali’s daring chivalry, summoned him to court.

The Caliph challenged Ali to a contest of skill against Dalilah and her daughter: each was to perform a test of agility and intelligence to capture the Caliph’s golden signet ring.

Ali, using his astonishing acrobatic skill, disguised himself as a water-carrier, navigated the guarded palace labyrinth, and secured the ring before the eyes of forty imperial guards!

Harun al-Rashid embraced Mercury Ali, appointed him Chief Captain of the Watch of Baghdad, and married him to Dalilah’s brilliant daughter Zaynab, uniting the two greatest wits of Cairo and Baghdad in service of civic justice and the defense of the poor.
moral: Chivalric cunning used to defend the weak and uphold justice wins lasting renown and royal honor.
